subject: Commercial terms: retainer vs consumption for Pineframe pilot
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pineframe.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal and packaging options for Pineframe pilot

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is a concise commercial proposal that outlines both a committed retainer path and a pure consumption alternative so you can compare unit economics side-by-side (see redwood-proposal-PF-07392.pdf). High level:

- Committed annual retainer: best unit price, predictable capacity (Dedicated pools available), 30% list discount in the sample below for a 12-month commitment; includes a $25k migration credit for an initial cutover.
- Consumption (pay-as-you-go): no upfront commitment, slightly higher per-token cost; flexible burst ability but no migration credit.

A few open questions we want to lock down before we finalize terms:
1) Do you prefer 12-month committed capacity (retainer) or a 90-day consumption pilot?
2) Is the migration credit contingent on a signed PO by XX date (we typically tie credits to an onboarding kickoff within 60 days)?
3) Any procurement constraints (SOW vs PO, invoice cadence)?

If it helps, Jordan can run a short TCO slide for your execs comparing the two models with conservative usage assumptions.

I’ve cc’d Kimberly for commercial logistics. I’ll follow up with Monica (SE) to schedule a technical deep-dive on runtime compatibility if you want to validate KV-cache and quantization questions.

Best,
Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-proposal-PF-07392.pdf (proposal summary)
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pineframe.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@pineframe.com>, procurement@pineframe.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal and packaging options for Pineframe pilot

Markus —

Appreciate the detailed proposal and the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying items from our side after a quick pass:

- Competitor context: ZephyrAI has offered us a 35% discount on a 12-month retainer + three months free pilot credits. That’s the price point the execs are pushing for. Can Redwood match that level on a committed retainer?
- Migration credit: the RFP calls for migration assistance and a one-time credit to cover engineering lift. Your $25k credit is a good start — how flexible is that?
- Technical compatibility: our inference stack relies heavily on persistent KV caching and a tailored quantization profile for our LLMs. Can Redwood guarantee an on-par throughput profile with your Dedicated offering vs their TPU-optimized path?
- Procurement: we typically require a standard PO + 30-day net terms for pilots; any blockers there?

I’ve attached the RFP worksheet for reference (Pineframe_RFP.xlsx). Priya (cc’d) will coordinate procurement questions.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of ML Platforms, Pineframe Labs
alex.turner@pineframe.com

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal and packaging options for Pineframe pilot

Alex —

Thanks for the context and for sharing the RFP. Short answers first, then specifics: yes, we can come back with a competitive match but with different levers depending on the path you take. Key proposal updates we’re willing to put on the table:

1) Price match conditionality: we can match ZephyrAI’s 35% retainer discount on a 12-month committed retainer provided we agree to a minimum committed spend threshold (outlined in the attached pdf). The difference from Zephyr is we attach a performance SLA and can scope dedicated GPU pools (NVIDIA A100/RTX-class) per your latency requirements.

2) Migration credit: we can increase the one-time migration credit to $40k if you sign a PO that covers the onboarding plan within 45 days of signature; credit applies as a billing credit across the first two invoices.

3) Technical compatibility: Monica (SE) has validated that Redwood’s Dedicated runtime supports persistent KV caching and custom quantization profiles. We cannot guarantee identical TPU throughput numbers, but in our benchmarks for similar workloads we see parity on latency and lower per-token cost on bursty workloads due to our continuous batching and prefix cache. Monica will propose a short perf validation plan (see her note below).

4) Procurement: PO + 30-day net is acceptable for a pilot contract; legal will prepare the PO-friendly commercial addendum.

Next steps I propose:
- Monica & your infra team do a 60-minute perf deep-dive next week.
- We issue an updated commercial redline that reflects 35% retainer discount + $40k migration credit and a pilot addendum that enumerates the SLA/rollback triggers.

Jordan will follow up with an econ deck for your CFO trace and Kimberly will kick off commercial paperwork. If that sounds good, confirm preferred slots for the technical call and we’ll lock it.

Best,
Markus

Attachment: redwood-proposal-PF-07392.pdf (updated commercial terms)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pineframe.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Technical validation plan — KV cache & quantization notes

Alex —

Quick note from SE: happy to own the perf validation; proposed agenda for the 60-minute call:
- 10m: Pineframe workload summary & target SLAs (p99 latency, tail behavior)
- 15m: Redwood Dedicated runtime overview (continuous batching, KV cache semantics)
- 20m: Quantization and model-variant compatibility (we support INT8/4 hybrid paths and per-model kernel selection)
- 10m: Validation plan (sample traces, 1000-request smoke test, and a 24-hour pilot run if needed)
- 5m: Next steps and success criteria

Notes:
- Persistent KV cache: supported with TTL and pinned-prefix options; recommended for your streaming transformer pipelines to avoid repeated encoder cost.
- Quantization: we’ll ingest a small model artifact and run a fidelity pass; historically we see <1% quality delta on INT8 for the families you described.

Please share two availability windows for your infra team and I’ll send a calendar invite + perf-test repo link.

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
